decision_summary: The Little Rock Board of Directors considered a resolution on October 21, 2025 to renew LRPD's Flock Safety software subscription for two one-year terms at $345,000 per year ($690,000 total) via Insight Public Sector. LRPD has used Flock Falcon LPR cameras since 2020, and the board previously approved 75 additional cameras in 2023.
notes: Primary city documents. Exact fleet camera count not stated in the renewal docs (75 additional Falcons purchased in 2023 per Res. 15,892/16,055); cameras left null. The Oct 2025 item is a board communication recommending adoption; final vote outcome not independently confirmed in the fetched text. $345,000/yr is the stated annual rate, not derived.

decision_summary: On August 27, 2026, FSPD announced tightened Flock policies: retention cut from 30 to 7 days, outside-agency search access disabled, and searches limited to felonies, domestic battery within 12 hours, and missing persons. The department notified Flock it will review whether to renew; the existing contract runs through November 30, 2027, with any renewal subject to public Board of Directors review.
notes: 21 is the ALPR camera count; the city reports 44 cameras total integrated with Flock OS (21 ALPR + 23 live-view, incl. WCCTV trailers). FSPD quoted $3,000/camera/yr and $12,500/trailer/yr unit rates but no exact total; annual cost left null rather than derived. An internal audit of FSPD Flock use was still underway as of Aug 2026.

decision_summary: Greers Ferry contracted with Flock Safety for five cameras, including one installed across from residents Charlie and Angie Wolf's home in May 2025. decision_summary: In early August 2026, Cabot Mayor Ken Kincade suspended the city's Flock Safety camera deployment over citizen privacy concerns. All cameras were taken offline (unplugged and covered) pending a comprehensive review and public input on whether to end the program permanently.
notes: Status is pending, not cancelled: suspension is mayoral and under review, with no final termination confirmed. Contract status during suspension is unknown. Police Chief John Dodd is leading the review; outside agencies were cut off from the system.

decision_summary: The Centerton City Council voted unanimously in August 2026 to terminate the city's Flock Safety contract after residents raised concerns about performance, privacy, and data access.
